question.worked_solution:
Here, we take out a factor of $3$ from the numerator and from the denominator, and then use the polynomial factorization ${t}^{2}-10t+25=(t-5)^{2}.$ Canceling out any common factors that appear in both the numerator and the denominator, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{3t-15}{3{t}^{2}-30t+75} & =\frac{3(t-5)}{3({t}^{2}-10t+25)} \\  & =\frac{3(t-5)}{3(t-5)^{2}} \\  & =\frac{3(t-5)}{3(t-5)(t-5)} \\  & =\frac{\cancel{3}\cancel{(t-5)}}{\cancel{3}\cancel{(t-5)}(t-5)} \\  & =\frac{1}{t-5}.\end{aligned}
$$
